answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity—whether labeled lotus, anchor, or meadow—to complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings. In a Wesolowski VDF, each next value depends on the previous one, so GPUs cannot materially shorten an individual chain through parallel computation. An attacker may run many chains concurrently, but each clone still incurs the full physical delay and computational cost; the proof lets others verify completion efficiently.
